title: Just Fill it!
description: A Chrome and Safari extension that turns the job page you're on into a tailored resume or cover letter and drops the PDF straight into the application.
hmw: tailor every application without ever leaving the job page?

facts.label: My part
facts.value: Designed and built it, for my own job search

facts.label: Built on
facts.value: A browser extension, a local helper, and Claude

The Just Fill it! panel in Safari, in Liquid Glass, with a finished resume ready to attach

blocks.text: I already had an AI workflow that tailored my resume and cover letter to each posting. Everything around it was the problem: copy the link, switch to a terminal, chat past whatever broke, find the PDF in Finder, read it, switch back, and pick the right file out of several drafts in a file picker. That was roughly 15 steps, four app switches and two file pickers per document, twice per job.
Designing for myself made the brief unusually sharp: I should never have to leave the job page.
One panel, on the page you're already on

items: Everything happens in a panel on the job page. No terminal, no Finder, no file picker.
The panel never submits anything. It hands you a file you can read, drag or attach, with notes on what it couldn't honestly claim.
A free-text box takes this run's instructions ("lead with design systems") instead of a back-and-forth chat.
It survives reloads and page changes, and keeps your last 10 documents, each linked to the job it was written for.

blocks.text: One product, drawn in each browser's own design language: Material 3 in Chrome and Liquid Glass in Safari.

images.alt: The panel in Safari, Liquid Glass

sections.label: Fast enough to use every time

blocks.text: A resume takes about 15 seconds and about 13,000 tokens, and a second document for the same job a few minutes later reuses most of that from cache. Cheap and quick enough to run on every application.
